title: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic concepts of sustainable farming systems

lessons.title: What sustainable farming means
lessons.html:
Farming for today and tomorrow

Sustainable means something can carry on for a long time. Sustainable farming means growing food and keeping animals in a way that:

  • Looks after the land: soil, water, veld, plants and animals.
  • Looks after the people: farm workers, their families and the community.
  • Makes enough money so the farm can keep going.

All three are needed. A farm that makes money but destroys its soil will fail in time. A farm that looks after the soil but loses money will also fail.

What happens when farming is not sustainable

Bad practiceWhat happens
Too many animals on the veldGood grass dies, soil is bare, dongas form
Ploughing up and down a slopeRain washes the soil away
Same crop every year in the same fieldSoil gets tired, pests and diseases build up
Too much fertiliser and sprayRivers get polluted, helpful insects die
Wasting waterDams and boreholes run dry
Unsafe work, poor payWorkers get hurt, leave, and skills are lost

The soil is alive

Good soil is full of life: earthworms, insects, fungi and tiny bacteria. They break down dead leaves and manure and make food for plants. Dark soil with lots of organic matter holds water like a sponge. When we look after soil life, crops grow better and need less fertiliser.

Water is precious

South Africa is a dry country. Many areas get little rain, and droughts come often. Every drop counts. Farms must use water carefully and keep rivers and dams clean.

lessons.title: Simple sustainable practices
lessons.html:
What we can do

For the soil

  • Keep the soil covered with plants, crop residues or mulch.
  • Rotate crops – change the crop in a field each season. For example, grow beans after maize. Beans add nitrogen to the soil.
  • Add compost and manure to feed soil life.
  • Plough and plant across the slope, along the contour, not up and down.
  • Plough less where the farm uses conservation agriculture.

For the veld and animals

  • Keep the right number of animals for the veld.
  • Move animals between camps so the grass can rest and grow again.
  • Fix small erosion ditches early with stones or branches.
  • Treat animals kindly and keep them healthy.

For water

  • Fix leaking pipes, taps and troughs.
  • Irrigate only as instructed.
  • Keep chemicals, fuel and dung heaps away from rivers and boreholes.
  • Do not wash spray tanks in rivers or dams.

For plants and wildlife

  • Leave some natural veld and trees. Bees, birds and helpful insects live there.
  • Do not kill owls, snakes and other animals that eat rats and pests.
  • Help remove alien plants such as wattle and prickly pear when the farm clears them.
  • Spray only when the supervisor says, with the right product and protective clothing.

For people

  • Work safely and help others work safely.
  • Share your knowledge with new workers.
  • Keep living areas clean.

Reduce waste

  • Make compost from plant waste and manure.
  • Put plastic, tins and old pipes in the right bins for recycling.
  • Switch off lights and pumps when not needed.

Key points

  • Sustainable farming looks after land, people and money together.
  • Keep soil covered, rotate crops and add compost.
  • Keep the right number of animals and rest the veld.
  • Save water and keep it clean.
  • Protect helpful wildlife and reduce waste.
